prompt:
Decide whether this exchange contains a motte-and-bailey move.

Structure: a speaker makes Claim A. A different person challenges it (Challenge C). The ORIGINAL speaker replies with Claim B.

Label MOTTE_BAILEY if Claim B retreats to a narrower, weaker or more easily defensible position than Claim A, while presenting that retreat as if it still defends Claim A (treating the weaker claim as equivalent to the original one).
Label NONE if Claim B is an honest clarification, adds detail, restates the same position, or openly concedes the point. Ordinary disagreement or clarification is NONE.

Claim A: [Content note: depictions of sexual violence in media] Showrunners are free to make creative choices and audiences are free to judge them by their own standards; I'm not even saying these particular rape scenes are unacceptable to me, just outlining the standard I use to judge them.

Challenge C: Your stated standard is so demanding/unrealistic that virtually no version of the scene could ever satisfy it, making the criticism unfalsifiable and not constructive.

Claim B: [Cites specific well-regarded examples of rape scenes in other films as done 'well', argues about diminishing narrative impact from overuse] I'm not saying they should avoid using rape scenes at all because it might trigger some viewers -- I'm saying they should avoid OVERUSING it, because that makes the rest of the audience jaded.

Respond with exactly this JSON: {"label": "MOTTE_BAILEY" or "NONE", "reason": "<one sentence>"}
